subject.title: [Feature]: Thread replies when agent uses tools; top-level for conversational responses

question: Should Slack add a default-off tool-use-sensitive automatic reply policy, and how should it interact with replyToMode, per-channel overrides, DMs/group DMs, existing threads, explicit top-level opt-outs, and streaming/status indicators?
rationale: The requested behavior adds a new config surface and changes reply-placement policy; source inspection shows no existing canonical precedence rule that automation can safely infer.

options.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
options.body: Define the config name and precedence, then implement it in Slack-owned config, routing, documentation, and regression/live proof with the default preserving current behavior.

options.title: Use static reply modes only
options.body: Keep account, chat-type, and per-channel replyToMode as the supported controls and close this request as not planned.

options.title: Defer to a broader reply-placement design
options.body: Wait for a cross-channel policy that can decide whether tool-use-sensitive placement belongs in Slack only or in a shared channel contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
recommendation.body: Define the config name and precedence, then implement it in Slack-owned config, routing, documentation, and regression/live proof with the default preserving current behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on Slack reply routing, thread safety, and per-channel reply mode behavior.
